name: Finding Adjacent Consecutive Numbers in a Sequence of Integers
description: Construct a program that checks whether a sequence of integers, entered one at a time, contains adjacent integers that are consecutive. The user enters -1 to indicate the end of the input.\nNote that integers which follow each other in order, without gaps, from smallest to largest are consecutive numbers. For example, 12, 13, 14 and 15 are consecutive numbers.
code:
#Step 1: Read the first integer that the user enters
text = input("Enter an integer: ")
num = int(text)
#Step 2: Read the rest of the integers that the user enters and check for adjacent consecutive numbers
while num != -1 :
    previous = num
    text = input("Enter an integer: ")
    num = int(text)
    if num != -1 and num - previous == 1 :
        print(previous, "and", num, "are consecutive.")

1.content: #Step 1: Read the first integer that the user enters

commentList: We need to read and process the first integer that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the first integer. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int().

Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer.

4.content: #Step 2: Read the rest of the integers that the user enters and check for adjacent consecutive numbers

commentList: We need to repeat receiving the integers from the user as long as the user enters an integer that is different from -1. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the input integer is different from -1.

The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters an integer that is different from -1. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to False, that is when the user enters -1.
We store the integer that the user entered in a variable called previous because we want to later compare it with the next integer that user will enter to check if they are consecutive numbers.

We need to read and process the next integer that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the next integer. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int().

Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer.

We need to test if the integer that the user entered is different from -1 because -1 indicates the end of the input and we need to skip it. We also need to test whether the integer that the user entered and its previous integer are consecutive numbers. To determine if the two integers are consecutive we need to test whether the difference between the two integers is 1 (consecutive numbers must differ by 1).

If the integer that the user entered is different from -1 and differs by 1 from its previous integer, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
Note that the and operator yields the result True if both conditions are True.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream, the two adjacent integers that are consecutive.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
